mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day returns: lower rates compress discount rates and increase liquidity, predicting positive returns when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 9.5%, it signals heightened recession risk and reduced corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5%, or the rank IC between UNRATE and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 218.5) indicates stable monetary policy, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day returns through reduced risk premia.
failure_condition: The joint condition occurs in more than 30% of instances where SPX 20-day returns are negative, or the interaction term in a regression of returns on FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL is not significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.5%), S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns due to recession-driven earnings declines and risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5%, or the rank IC between UNRATE and returns in high unemployment regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600, it indicates weak consumer demand and economic slowdown, predicting negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 600, or the rank IC between HOUST and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) is inversely related to S&P 500 5-day returns: lower output signals economic weakness, predicting negative returns over a short horizon.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations when INDPRO < 100, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 218.5) indicates stable monetary policy, predicting positive S&P 500 60-day returns through sustained equity valuation support.
failure_condition: The joint condition occurs in more than 30% of instances where SPX 60-day returns are negative, or the interaction term in a regression of returns on FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL is not significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In weak demand regimes (HOUST < 600), S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 600, or the rank IC between HOUST and 60-day returns in weak demand regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
